How do I sort a stack of cards?

  1. Photograph each card separately, or select separate card images from your gallery. Add up to 10 images to the current queue.
  2. Review each suggested match. Confirm the set, full number, language and finish against the physical card.
  3. Set the raw condition or the grade already on a slab. Add confirmed cards and their quantities to your collection.
  4. Confirm or remove the queued results before starting the next group. Check the remaining free allowance or current Premium access in the app.

The queue does not read a whole binder page or continuously take photos. If a result is wrong, search for the exact printing before saving it. If no exact record or price is available, keep that information unresolved; do not substitute another printing or treat a missing price as zero.

The bottleneck is entry, not identification

Looking up a single card is easy and always has been. What defeats people is volume: a few thousand cards, most of them low value, with the ones that matter buried somewhere inside.

A batch card scanner is built for that shape of problem. Add up to 10 camera captures or gallery selections to the current queue, review each suggested match, then continue with the next batch. It does not continuously auto-capture cards or read an entire binder page in one shot.

Find the keepers inside the bulk

Most of a collection is worth very little and a small part carries almost all the value. You cannot tell which is which until everything is identified and priced.

Scanning the whole stack surfaces that split, so the cards worth sleeving, grading or selling stop being invisible.

Everything lands in one collection

Each result enters Review with its matching card record. Confirm the card, choose its finish and language, and set a raw condition or existing slab grade before adding it to your collection. There is no separate spreadsheet or import step to reconcile.

Bulk card scanner questions.

How many free scans does Card AI include?

Free access includes a lifetime total of 10 successful scans. It does not reset each day or month. A separate queue holds up to 10 images at a time; it does not provide extra free scans. Check the current Premium offer in the app for its price and terms.

Can I scan multiple cards at once?

You can queue up to 10 separate camera or gallery images. Review each card, then confirm or remove the results before the next group. This is not one-photo recognition of an entire binder page, and each scan still uses the applicable free allowance or Premium access.

Do I have to confirm each card?

Scan results are reviewed before they are added, which is where you confirm the printing and set the condition or grade for each card.

Does bulk scanning work across different games?

Yes. Cards from supported games can share the same collection, so a mixed stack of supported categories does not need a separate collection for each game.

Is this an AI card scanner or manual entry?

The AI TCG card scanner suggests likely catalog matches; you confirm the matching card, finish and language, then set condition or grade before adding it. That review step keeps a fast batch run grounded in the card you actually own.
